cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; small change helps at tapas bars. Tipping is optional, rounding up is enough.
name: Córdoba
tagline: The great mosque, flower-filled patios and Moorish lanes
summary: Córdoba was once the largest city in Western Europe and the capital of Islamic Spain. Walk the forest of red-and-white arches in the Mezquita, cross the Roman bridge at sunset, peek into flower-filled patios in the old Jewish quarter and ride out to the ruined palace city of Medina Azahara.
seasonNote: Spring is best, and May brings the patio festival; July and August often pass 40°C.
arrival: High-speed AVE trains reach Córdoba from Madrid in 1h45 and from Seville in 45 minutes; the station is a 20-minute walk from the old town.
gettingAround: The old town is small and walkable; take a bus or tour to Medina Azahara.
foodTip: Salmorejo (thick cold tomato soup), flamenquín (rolled fried pork and ham) and rabo de toro (oxtail stew).
buyTip: Embossed leather (guadamecí) and silver filigree from the Judería workshops.

connections.note: AVE high-speed trains several times an hour.

items.name: Mosque–Cathedral (Mezquita)
items.summary: A vast 8th-century mosque of striped horseshoe arches with a Renaissance cathedral built into its heart.
items.expect: Paid; mass times close it to visitors on Sunday mornings.
items.tip: Come at the free early-morning entry (Mon to Sat, 8:30 to 9:20) for near silence.
items.why: One of the world's great buildings.

items.name: Roman Bridge and Calahorra Tower
items.summary: The arched bridge over the Guadalquivir with the old town skyline behind it.
items.expect: Free to cross; the tower museum is paid.
items.tip: Cross at sunset and look back at the Mezquita.

items.name: Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos
items.summary: Fortress-palace with terraced gardens of pools, cypresses and orange trees.
items.tip: Climb the towers for a view over the gardens.

items.name: Judería and Calleja de las Flores
items.summary: Whitewashed lanes, the tiny medieval synagogue and the flower-pot alley framing the Mezquita tower.
items.tip: Go early or late for the alley photo.

items.name: Palacio de Viana
items.summary: Noble palace with twelve different patios full of flowers and fountains.
items.tip: Visit in spring when the patios are in bloom.

items.name: Medina Azahara
items.summary: Ruins of a 10th-century caliph's palace city on the hills west of town.
items.expect: Shuttle bus from town; closed Mondays.
items.tip: Start at the museum, then the shuttle up to the ruins.
flow: Ruins and Hall of Abd al-Rahman.

items.name: Templo Romano and Plaza de la Corredera
items.summary: Arcaded 17th-century square with cafés, near the columns of a Roman temple.
items.tip: Have breakfast churros under the arcades.

items.name: Salmorejo
items.summary: Córdoba's thick cold tomato and bread soup topped with ham and egg.
items.tip: Try it at Taberna Salinas or any old taberna.

items.name: Bodegas Mezquita
items.summary: Reliable tavern near the Mezquita for Córdoba classics and Montilla wines.
items.tip: Order a few medias raciones to share.

items.name: Mercado Victoria
items.summary: A 19th-century iron pavilion turned food hall with tapas and drinks stalls.
items.tip: Good for a quick dinner of many small plates.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; service is included in prices, so round up only for good service.
name: Mont-Saint-Michel
tagline: The abbey island rising from the tides of Normandy
summary: Mont-Saint-Michel is a rocky island crowned by a medieval abbey, cut off by some of the biggest tides in Europe. Climb the single village street to the abbey, walk the bay barefoot with a guide at low tide, and pair it with Saint-Malo's walled port and the D-Day beaches of Normandy.
seasonNote: Spring and September are quieter; the big spring tides (around full and new moon) are the most dramatic.
arrival: Trains run from Paris to Rennes or Pontorson, then a bus to the Mont; driving from Paris takes about 4 hours.
gettingAround: Park on the mainland and take the free shuttle or walk 45 minutes across the causeway; a car helps for Saint-Malo and the D-Day beaches.
foodTip: La Mère Poulard's puffy omelette, pré-salé lamb from the salt meadows, Cancale oysters and Breton crêpes.
buyTip: Butter biscuits and salted-caramel from the village, and cider and Calvados from Normandy farms.
baseArea: Hotels by the shuttle stop, or stay on the Mont for the evening calm

connections.note: TGV to Rennes, then bus to the Mont.

items.name: Mont-Saint-Michel Abbey
items.summary: Gothic abbey at the summit, with the cloister hanging over the bay.
items.tip: Book a timed ticket and go late afternoon when day-trippers leave.

items.name: Grande Rue and the ramparts
items.summary: The one crowded village street, then quieter ramparts with views over the sands.
items.tip: Take the ramparts up and the street down.

items.name: Causeway and Barrage view
items.summary: Walk the bridge-causeway with the Mont growing in front of you; the dam viewpoint is great at night.
items.tip: Walk out, shuttle back; stay for the lights after dark.

items.name: Guided bay walk at low tide
items.summary: Barefoot walk across the sands with a licensed guide, learning about quicksand and the tides.
items.expect: Only with a guide; tides are dangerous.
items.tip: Book with a licensed guide in Genêts or on the Mont.
items.why: See the Mont as pilgrims did.

items.name: Saint-Malo
items.summary: Walled corsair port with rampart walks, tidal pools and Fort National reachable at low tide.
items.tip: Walk the full ramparts circuit, then crêpes inside the walls.

items.name: Omaha Beach and the American Cemetery
items.summary: The D-Day landing beach and the cliff-top cemetery above it.
items.tip: Pair with Pointe du Hoc nearby.

items.name: Omelette at La Mère Poulard
items.summary: The famous whisked omelette cooked over a wood fire since 1888.
items.tip: Watch the cooks beating eggs in copper bowls by the door.

items.name: Pré-salé lamb
items.summary: Lamb raised on the salt meadows around the bay, tender with a light salty flavour.
items.expect: Look for "agneau de pré-salé" on menus.
items.tip: Mainland restaurants are better value than on the Mont.

items.name: Oysters at Cancale
items.summary: Stalls by the harbour wall sell oysters by the dozen to eat on the steps.
items.tip: Throw the shells onto the beach like the locals.
flow: Buy a dozen at the stalls.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; service is included in prices, so round up only for good service.
name: Chamonix
tagline: Mont Blanc, glaciers and the Aiguille du Midi
summary: Chamonix sits at the foot of Mont Blanc, the highest mountain in Western Europe. Ride the cable car up the Aiguille du Midi to 3,842 m, take the rack railway to the Mer de Glace glacier, hike to Lac Blanc for the mirror view of the range, and ski or paraglide in one of the world's great mountain towns.
seasonNote: December to April for skiing, June to September for hiking; many lifts close in May and November.
arrival: Geneva Airport is 1h15 by shuttle bus; trains connect via Saint-Gervais.
gettingAround: Free local buses and trains in the valley with your guest card; lifts and cable cars to the heights.
foodTip: Tartiflette, fondue savoyarde, raclette and diots (Savoy sausages).
buyTip: Beaufort and Reblochon cheese and Génépi liqueur.
baseArea: Chamonix centre near the Aiguille du Midi station

connections.note: Airport shuttles several times a day.
Mont Blanc Express via Martigny, then Visp.

items.name: Aiguille du Midi
items.summary: Cable car to a needle at 3,842 m with the glass Step into the Void box.
items.expect: Expensive; cloud hides everything on bad days.
items.tip: Check the summit webcam and go on the first cars.
items.why: Face to face with Mont Blanc.
items.book: Book a time slot in summer

items.name: Montenvers and the Mer de Glace
items.summary: Rack railway to France's largest glacier and an ice cave carved into it each year.
items.expect: Hundreds of steps down to the ice cave; signs mark how far the ice has retreated.
items.tip: Look for the yearly markers on the walk down.

items.name: Lac Blanc hike
items.summary: Hike to an alpine lake that mirrors the whole Mont Blanc range.
items.expect: About 3h round trip from the Flégère lift; summer only.
items.tip: Go early for still water and fewer people.

items.name: Le Brévent
items.summary: Cable car to a balcony directly facing Mont Blanc.
items.expect: Less busy than the Aiguille du Midi.
items.tip: Paragliders launch here; watch them take off.
items.why: The best full view of the massif.

items.name: Paragliding tandem flight
items.summary: Fly with an instructor from Planpraz down to the valley floor.
items.tip: Morning flights are smoother.
items.book: Book a day or two ahead

items.name: Chamonix town centre
items.summary: Alpine town of chalets, outdoor shops and the statue of Saussure pointing at Mont Blanc.
items.tip: Stroll the river Arve and the church square.

items.name: Skyway Monte Bianco
items.summary: Rotating cable car on the Italian side, through the Mont Blanc Tunnel.
items.expect: Bring your passport; 20 minutes by car via the tunnel.
items.tip: Combine with lunch in Courmayeur.

items.name: Tartiflette
items.summary: Potatoes, bacon and onions baked under melted Reblochon.
items.tip: Pair with a crisp Savoie white wine.

items.name: Fondue savoyarde
items.summary: Pot of melted Beaufort, Comté and white wine for dipping bread.
items.tip: La Calèche and Le Monchu are classic spots.

items.name: Le Refuge du Lac Blanc
items.summary: Mountain hut by the lake serving drinks and simple hot meals.
items.tip: A drink on the terrace after the hike.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; service is included in prices, so round up only for good service.
name: Annecy
tagline: Canals, a turquoise lake and the Alps of Savoie
summary: Annecy is a pastel old town of canals and flower boxes on one of Europe's cleanest lakes. Photograph the island-prison Palais de l'Isle, cycle or swim around Lake Annecy, take the boat to Talloires, and drive up the Semnoz or the Col de la Forclaz for paragliders and big Alpine views.
seasonNote: June to September for swimming; the Tuesday, Friday and Sunday markets run year round.
arrival: Trains from Paris take 3h40; Geneva Airport is 45 minutes by bus or car.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; bike the lakeside path or take the lake boats.
foodTip: Reblochon (made nearby), lake fish like féra, and Savoie wines.
buyTip: Reblochon and Tomme de Savoie from the old-town market.
baseArea: Vieille Ville or near the lake

items.name: Palais de l'Isle and the canals
items.summary: 12th-century island prison in the Thiou canal, the town's famous image.
items.expect: Small museum inside; the view is the point.
items.tip: Photograph from Pont Perrière.

items.name: Lake Annecy
items.summary: Clear turquoise lake ringed by mountains, with public beaches.
items.expect: Water is cool even in summer.
items.tip: Rent a pedal boat or swim at Plage d'Albigny.

items.name: Pont des Amours
items.summary: Little bridge between the canal and the lake, said to bring lasting love.
items.tip: Look down the Vassé canal lined with boats.

items.name: Château d'Annecy
items.summary: Hilltop castle of the Counts of Geneva with a museum and town views.
items.tip: Go for the view over the rooftops.

items.name: Lake cycle path
items.summary: Flat bike path along the western shore toward Duingt and its castle.
items.tip: Return by lake boat with your bike.

items.name: Col de la Forclaz paragliding
items.summary: High pass above the lake where paragliders launch over the water.
items.tip: Watch from the café terrace even if you don't fly.

items.name: Old-town market
items.summary: Stalls along the canals selling Savoie cheese, sausages and produce.
items.tip: Sunday is biggest.

items.name: Raclette and Savoie dishes
items.summary: Melted cheese scraped over potatoes, charcuterie and pickles.
items.tip: Old-town restaurants on Rue Sainte-Claire.

items.name: Féra from the lake
items.summary: Delicate whitefish caught in Lake Annecy, pan-fried with butter and lemon.
items.tip: Order it at a lakeside restaurant with a glass of Roussette.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; Christmas market stalls may want cash.
name: Colmar
tagline: Half-timbered canals and the Alsace wine route
summary: Colmar is a storybook Alsace town of painted half-timbered houses and flower-lined canals. Drift through Little Venice by boat, see the Isenheim Altarpiece in the Unterlinden Museum, then follow the wine route to Riquewihr and Eguisheim, and come in December for some of France's best Christmas markets.
seasonNote: Late spring and the September harvest are lovely; Christmas markets run late November to late December and are crowded.
arrival: TGV trains from Paris take 2h20; Basel-Mulhouse airport is 45 minutes away.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; buses or a car (or bike) for the wine villages.
foodTip: Choucroute garnie, tarte flambée (flammekueche), baeckeoffe stew and kougelhopf cake, with Riesling and Gewürztraminer.
buyTip: Alsace wines, gingerbread and Munster cheese.

items.name: Little Venice (Petite Venise)
items.summary: Pastel houses and flower boxes along the Lauch canal.
items.tip: Take the 30-minute flat-bottomed boat ride.

items.name: Unterlinden Museum
items.summary: Former convent housing Grünewald's Isenheim Altarpiece.
items.tip: Spend time with the altarpiece panels.

items.name: Maison des Têtes and Maison Pfister
items.summary: Two famous Renaissance houses, one covered in carved faces, one with painted balconies.
items.tip: Walk Rue des Marchands between them.

items.name: Koïfhus and the Tanners' Quarter
items.summary: Old customs house with a tiled roof beside the tall tanners' houses.
items.tip: Pair with the covered market nearby.

items.name: Riquewihr
items.summary: Walled wine village of half-timbered houses among the vineyards.
items.tip: Taste in a family cellar, not the main-street shops.

items.name: Eguisheim
items.summary: Village built in concentric rings around a castle and chapel.
items.tip: Walk the outer ring lane.

items.name: Haut-Kœnigsbourg Castle
items.summary: Restored red-sandstone castle high above the Alsace plain.
items.tip: Go on a clear day for the view to the Black Forest.

items.name: Colmar Christmas markets
items.summary: Six markets spread across the old town's squares and canals.
items.expect: Late November to late December; crowded weekends.
items.tip: Go on a weekday evening.

items.name: Tarte flambée
items.summary: Thin crisp flatbread with cream, onions and bacon, baked in a wood oven.
items.tip: Order one to share, then a sweet one with apples.

items.name: Choucroute garnie
items.summary: Sauerkraut piled with sausages, pork and potatoes, cooked in Riesling.
items.tip: Pair with an Alsace Riesling.

items.name: Marché Couvert
items.summary: 19th-century covered market by the canal with cheese, bread and food stalls.
items.tip: Grab a lunch plate and eat by the water.

cashTip: Cards are used everywhere, some places are card only. Tipping is a small round-up.
name: Rotterdam
tagline: Bold architecture, Europe's biggest port and windmills nearby
summary: Rebuilt after the war, Rotterdam is the Netherlands' boldest modern city. See the cube houses and the arched Markthal, cross the Erasmus Bridge, look into the mirrored Depot Boijmans art store, ride a water taxi to the harbour, and cycle out to the UNESCO windmills of Kinderdijk.
seasonNote: Summer is liveliest with festivals; winter is grey and windy.
arrival: Trains from Amsterdam take 40 minutes, from Schiphol 25; Eurostar runs from London.
gettingAround: Metro, trams and water taxis; bikes are the local way.
foodTip: Kibbeling (fried fish), stroopwafels, Surinamese and Indonesian food.
buyTip: Design pieces and Dutch cheese from the Markthal.

items.name: Markthal
items.summary: Arched market hall with a giant fruit-and-flowers mural across its ceiling.
items.tip: Look up from the centre for the full mural.

items.name: Cube Houses
items.summary: Tilted yellow cube homes on poles by Piet Blom; one is a show home.
items.tip: Visit the Kijk-Kubus to see how people live inside.

items.name: Erasmus Bridge
items.summary: White cable-stayed "Swan" bridge over the Maas.
items.tip: Walk across at sunset toward the Hotel New York.

items.name: Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen
items.summary: The world's first publicly accessible art storage, a mirrored bowl with a roof forest.
items.tip: Ride to the rooftop for the view.

items.name: Euromast
items.summary: 185 m observation tower with a rotating glass lift.
items.tip: Go up on a clear evening.

items.name: Port of Rotterdam boat tour
items.summary: Boat trip through Europe's biggest port among container ships and cranes.
items.tip: Sit on the open deck.

items.name: Kinderdijk windmills
items.summary: Nineteen 18th-century windmills along the polder canals.
items.expect: Paid to enter two mills; waterbus from Rotterdam.
items.tip: Take the Waterbus from Erasmusbrug.

items.name: Delfshaven
items.summary: The old harbour that survived the war, where the Pilgrims left for America.
items.tip: Have a beer at a canal-side pub.

items.name: Markthal food stalls
items.summary: Stalls selling cheese, stroopwafels, poffertjes and world food.
items.tip: Grab poffertjes and a fresh stroopwafel.

items.name: Kibbeling
items.summary: Battered chunks of white fish with garlic sauce from a fish stall.
items.tip: Saturday market at Binnenrotte has great stalls.

items.name: Fenix Food Factory area (Katendrecht)
items.summary: Old port peninsula of food spots and terraces facing the skyline.
items.tip: Take the ferry over from the Hotel New York side.

cashTip: Cards widely accepted; carry some koruna for small cafés. Tip about 10 percent.
name: Český Krumlov
tagline: A castle town in a loop of the Vltava
summary: Český Krumlov is a near-perfect medieval town curled inside a bend of the Vltava river, under a huge painted castle. Climb the castle tower, cross the cloak bridge, float the river in a raft or canoe, and wander lanes of red roofs that look much as they did 400 years ago.
seasonNote: Summer is warm and busy with day-trippers; evenings are quiet once tour buses leave.
arrival: Buses from Prague take about 3 hours; shuttles run from Vienna, Salzburg and Linz.
gettingAround: The old town is small and walkable; cobbles are steep in places.
foodTip: Roast pork with dumplings and sauerkraut, trout from local ponds and Eggenberg beer brewed in town.
buyTip: Czech glass and puppets, and Budweiser Budvar from nearby České Budějovice.
baseArea: Old town inside the river loop

items.name: Český Krumlov Castle
items.summary: Vast castle complex with painted courtyards, a bear moat and a working Baroque theatre.
items.expect: Interior tours paid and timed; closed in winter except some areas.
items.tip: Book the Baroque theatre tour for a rare sight.

items.name: Castle Tower
items.summary: Painted Renaissance tower with the classic view over the red roofs and river loop.
items.tip: Go late in the day for golden light.

items.name: Cloak Bridge and castle gardens
items.summary: Multi-storey covered bridge leading to formal gardens and a rotating open-air theatre.
items.tip: Walk through to the fountain at the far end.

items.name: Old town lanes
items.summary: Medieval lanes, the town square and St. Vitus Church inside the river bend.
items.tip: Explore early morning and evening.

items.name: Vltava rafting
items.summary: Paddle a canoe or raft through the town and over the little weirs.
items.expect: Summer only; you may get wet.
items.tip: Short town loops take about an hour.
items.why: See the town from the water.

items.name: Egon Schiele Art Centrum
items.summary: Gallery about the painter Egon Schiele, who lived here, with modern art shows.
items.tip: Combine with the Seminary Garden view.

items.name: Hluboká Castle
items.summary: White neo-Gothic castle in an English park.
items.tip: Combine with beer in České Budějovice.

items.name: Czech roast pork and dumplings
items.summary: Roast pork, bread dumplings and sauerkraut, the national dish.
items.tip: Old-town taverns serve it with local beer.

items.name: Krčma v Šatlavské
items.summary: Candle-lit medieval tavern grilling meat over an open fire.
items.tip: Ask for a table in the vaulted cellar.

items.name: Eggenberg Brewery
items.summary: Town brewery since the 1500s with a beer hall and tours.
items.tip: Try the unfiltered lager.
